add.text: Notoungulates make up over half the described diversity of South America's native ungulates, with over 150 genera in 14 families.
Notoungulates were morphologically diverse, with forms resembling animals as different as rabbits and rhinoceroses.
Notoungulates and other native South American ungulates reached their apex of diversity during the Eocene and Oligocene.
Because the whole West Antarctic Ice Sheet is grounded below sea level, it is vulnerable to geologically rapid ice loss.
The West Antarctic ice sheet declined somewhat during the warm early Pliocene, about five to three million years ago, and the Ross Sea opened up.
During the Eocene, about 45 Ma, subduction of the Farallon plate along the Central American subduction zone was re-established.
The Sea of Japan is a modern example of back-arc spreading, a modest ocean basin opened between the volcanic arc of Japan and the Asian mainland.

Pinnipeds belong to the suborder Caniformia of the order Carnivora; their closest living relatives are musteloids (weasels, raccoons, skunks and red pandas), from which they diverged about 50 million years ago.
Africa was relatively isolated and kept its endemic fauna.
The change from aragonite to calcite seas was not simple but a protracted and variable change through the Cambrian.
Calcite seas coincided with times of rapid seafloor spreading and global greenhouse climate.
Hardgrounds were very common in calcite seas such as those of the Ordovician and Jurassic, but virtually absent from the aragonite seas of the Permian.
With each sea-level rise, most of North America was covered by a shallow tropical ocean.
Paleo-Tethys lay between Gondwana and the Hunic terranes, continental fragments that broke off Gondwana and moved north.
The Hunic terranes are divided into the European Hunic (crust under parts of Europe, called Armorica, and Iberia) and the Asiatic Hunic (crust of parts of southern Asia).
In the Early Carboniferous a subduction zone developed south of the European Hunic terranes, consuming Paleo-Tethys oceanic crust.
Trilobites were hit hard by the end-Ordovician mass extinction and went extinct in the end-Permian mass extinction.
The soft-tissue detail in Beecher's trilobite-type preservation comes from pyritization, where soft tissues are replaced with pyrite.
In pyritized trilobites the mineral pyrite, FeS2, has replaced the hard parts that made up the trilobite.
The Deccan Traps may originally have covered about 1.5 million km2, with a correspondingly larger original volume.
The region was reduced by erosion and plate tectonics, and the present area of directly observable lava flows is around 500,000 km2.
Later proboscideans are distinguished by enormous size, tusks and long muscular trunks, which were less developed or absent in early proboscideans.
By the Early Eocene, proboscideans began growing in size.
Among modern groups, Lepidosauria is the sister taxon to Archelosauria, which includes turtles, birds and crocodilians.
Lepidosauria splits into Squamata and Rhynchocephalia.
The earliest modern lepidosaurs are known from the Middle Jurassic, though Megachirella from the Middle Triassic may be a stem-group squamate.
The Aidaralash GSSP marks the Carboniferous-Permian boundary and the base of the Asselian.
The collision of Patagonia was followed by the rifting and eventual breakup of Gondwana in the early Mesozoic, which rotated the Patagonian landmass on a large scale.

One theory has all of Patagonia arriving from Gondwana as an allochthonous landmass in the Paleozoic; the other holds that Northern Patagonia is autochthonous and only the southern part is allochthonous.
Dimetrodon was probably the top predator of the Red Beds ecosystem, feeding on animals such as the shark Xenacanthus and the amphibians Trimerorhachis and Diplocaulus.
The term pelycosaurs, traditionally used for Dimetrodon, is now considered obsolete and replaced by terms such as primitive or basal synapsids.
The Dobele crater is not exposed at the surface.
The Mangrullo Formation yields several fossil embryos, a hatchling and very small mesosaurids, the oldest known evidence of amniotic ontogeny.
In the top layers the sea connection was reestablished, and mesosaur fossils disappeared, replaced again by fish and bioturbating organisms.
The Ternovka crater is not exposed at the surface.
Global diversity rose dramatically in the Capitanian, probably as disaster taxa filled empty guilds, then fell again in the Wuchiapingian after the end-Guadalupian event.
A significant mass extinction at the end of the Capitanian was associated with ocean anoxia and acidification, and possibly caused by the volcanic eruptions that produced the Emeishan Traps.
Callistophytales lived from the Pennsylvanian to the Permian.

They were reproductively more sophisticated than most other Paleozoic seed ferns, some of which they seem to have out-competed and replaced in the coal swamp vegetation during the Late Pennsylvanian and Permian.
The weigeltisaurid gliding membrane originated on the lower-lateral surface of the body, unlike those of rib-gliding reptiles.

A 2011 study found Coelurosauravus a less efficient glider than modern Draco because of its larger body size, but a 2025 study found its body mass had been overestimated and it would have been a relatively efficient glider.

The estimated energy of the Araguainha impact is insufficient to directly cause the global mass extinction, but the huge local rifting would have released large amounts of oil and gas from the shattered rock.
The impact punched through Paleozoic sedimentary units of the Paraná Basin and exposed the underlying Ordovician granite basement.
